headline: Google DeepMind and GovTech deliver an on-device scam detection model
body: Google DeepMind and GovTech, the Government Technology Agency of Singapore, say their collaboration delivers an on-device scam detection model. Google DeepMind's Gemma model was fine-tuned on local scam conversations, including impersonations of banks, and the model triggers a real-time warning when it detects manipulative patterns. Scams make up over half of Singapore’s reported crimes, and account for more than S$4 billion in losses since 2019.
note: Google says messaging platforms and operating system vendors can integrate these models directly, so banks tracking impersonation scams may want to watch where the model turns up next.

evidence.text: The collaboration delivers an on-device scam detection model that helps protect citizens without compromising privacy.
To address this, Google DeepMind and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) have been working together as part of our National AI Partnership with the Singapore Government.
To address this, Google DeepMind's lightweight Gemma model was fine-tuned on local scam conversations.
These ranged from impersonations of public institutions, banks, and local figures, to trending regional schemes, ensuring the model can distinguish benign social chatter from genuine manipulation.

When the model detects manipulative conversational patterns, it triggers a real-time warning directly on the user's device advising them to pause and exercise caution before sharing sensitive information or funds.
Scams make up over half of Singapore’s reported crimes, and account for more than S$4 billion in losses since 2019.
Messaging platforms and operating system vendors can directly integrate these lightweight models to safeguard users locally, ensuring chat interactions remain secure without exposing private data.
